payload.text: Methodology defect found after the first baseline run (run id crypto_baseline_v1-01b546fd8f21): each trial was simulated as one continuous 33-month deployment, and the research rule that a drawdown or floor pause stops new entries for the rest of the run halted every trial within months, so the later validation and test windows held no trades and the walk-forward evaluation was uninformative. Correction, with no change to any rule, parameter, cost basis, fill assumption, dataset or split: each 3-month window is now an independent deployment from a fresh USD 50 ledger with two days of feature warm-up, positions open at a window end are closed at the last bar's estimated bid, and the continuous deployment is reported separately as the policy-pause diagnostic. The first run's RESULT events remain in this registry.

controls.rule: every test window, fresh USD 50 ledger, same costs: rule only; random rejection at the model's realised veto rate in that window (HashRandomReject, one salt per seed); equal accepted-candidate count per window (TurnoverMatchedReject, one salt per seed)

filter.inner_selection_metric: validation log-loss of the uncalibrated probability, scored by the exported numpy bundle (lowest wins; ties: the first grid point)
filter.label_definition: each candidate simulated alone through ResearchEngine from a fresh USD 50 ledger with the study policy, fee schedule and fill assumptions: marketable limit at the estimated ask plus the frozen offset, filled at the next bar open plus half-spread and slippage only within the limit and the TTL; stop before target inside a bar; time, session-close and stop-gap exits at the open; fees on both legs; a position open at the end of the supplied bars is closed at the last bar's estimated bid (END_OF_DATA). net_usd = net PnL rounded half-even to 12 dp (0 when not filled); net_return = net_usd / entry notional; win = net_usd > 0
filter.label_target: win = net USD after all costs > 0 (candidate simulated alone)
filter.threshold_rule: on validation only: among thresholds whose calibrated probability accepts at least min_accepts validation candidates, the one with the highest net PnL per session of an engine replay of the validation window (fresh USD 50 ledger, the study's policy, fees and fills; the bundle as ModelThresholdFilter accepting p >= threshold; outcome bars up to the test start); ties go to the lower threshold
filter.untrainable_fold: a fold without a trainable model (one outcome class, too few candidates, or no threshold with enough accepts) vetoes every candidate in its test window (fail closed: cash)

trial.selection_correction: Per walk-forward fold (purged and embargoed by the maximum hold): the scaler and model are fitted on training-window labels only; the grid point with the lowest validation log-loss is kept; the calibration map is fitted on validation scores; the threshold is chosen on validation by the net PnL per session of an engine replay of the validation window with the model filter (at least min_accepts accepted validation candidates; ties to the lower threshold). A fold that cannot be trained vetoes every candidate in its test window. The test window is never an input to training or selection. Each test window is replayed for: rule only, rule + model filter, random rejection at the model's realised veto rate (N salts) and equal accepted-candidate counts (N salts). Study walk-forward: per fold deploy the trial with the highest positive validation objective, else hold cash. A day trade pays the spread every day, so earlier years would test a cost that no longer exists. Nineteen months is one market regime.
trial.hypothesis: On Capital.com's Bitcoin and Ether CFDs, a regularised logistic veto (a LightGBM challenger per fold only when better on validation) of T-0023's hourly breakout signals, trained per rolling six-month fold on nine cfd-breakout-v1 features, gives test-window net results after the quoted spread, slippage and financing that beat the rule alone, random refusal at the filter's own refusal rate and equal-turnover refusal of the smallest breaks, in both the base and the stressed view, over 2025-10 to 2026-06 in independent three-month deployments from USD 100.

filter.challenger_rule: per fold, the challenger replaces the primary model only if its validation objective is strictly higher; a model that cannot be trained loses to one that can

controls.rule: every test window, fresh sleeve capital, base, stressed and diagnostic views: the rule alone; random refusal at the filter's realised refusal rate in that window (hash draw, one salt per seed); equal turnover, refusing as many signals as the filter did, the smallest break beyond the channel (in mean true ranges) first, ties by signal id

feature_definitions.break_atr: (mid close beyond the channel of the previous channel_hours bars) / mean true range of the last atr_hours bars, decision bar included; negative inside the channel
feature_definitions.hour_cos: cos(2 pi h / 24), h = UTC hour of the decision time
feature_definitions.hour_sin: sin(2 pi h / 24), h = UTC hour of the decision time
feature_definitions.hours_to_flat: hours from the decision time to the trade's flat time
feature_definitions.return_24h: side x ln(mid close / mid close 24 bars earlier)
feature_definitions.return_72h: side x ln(mid close / mid close 72 bars earlier)
feature_definitions.spread_bps: max(quoted spread at the decision bar's open, at its close) / mid close x 1e4
feature_definitions.vol_ratio_24_168: sd of the last 24 hourly log returns / sd of the last 168 (1 if zero)

filter.inner_selection_metric: validation log-loss of the uncalibrated probability, scored by the exported numpy bundle (lowest wins; ties: the first grid point)
filter.label_definition: an unfiltered base-view run of the frozen rule over the window emits every signal with its cfd-breakout-v1 features at its decision time; a signal the run took is labelled by its realised trade, any other by the same signal traded alone from the sleeve's capital with the same costs; win = net USD after spread, slippage and financing > 0; net return = net USD / notional. A signal still open when the outcome bars end, refused even alone, or with less than a week of earlier bars has no label.
filter.label_target: win = net USD after all costs > 0
filter.threshold_rule: on validation only: among thresholds whose calibrated probability accepts at least min_accepts validation signals, the one with the highest net USD per session of a base-view replay of the validation window (fresh sleeve capital, the base study's policy and costs, the bundle as the filter; outcome bars up to the test start); ties go to the lower threshold
filter.untrainable_fold: a fold without a trainable model (one outcome class, too few signals, or no threshold with enough accepts) refuses every signal in its test window (fail closed: cash)
filter.works_rule: the filter works only if its net USD beats the rule alone, the mean of the random control's seeds and the equal-turnover control, in the base view and in the stressed view

trial.selection_correction: Rolling walk-forward folds over the base study's development period, purged and embargoed by the rule's longest hold: training labels decided in the training window with outcomes before its end, purged within the embargo; validation labels decided in the validation window (less the embargo) with outcomes before the test start. Per fold the primary model is trained with training.train_fold (grid by validation log-loss, calibration on validation, threshold on validation by the net USD per session of a validation replay) and a challenger replaces it only with a strictly higher validation objective. A fold that cannot be trained refuses every test signal. The test window is never an input to training or selection. Each test window is replayed for the rule alone, the rule with the filter, random refusal at the filter's refusal rate (N salts) and equal turnover (smallest break refused first), in three cost views. Study walk forward: per fold the filtered rule when its validation objective is positive, else cash. Selection-aware checks: a reality check across the four variants and the deflated Sharpe ratio with N = all registered trials. The locked final test period is not used.
trial.universe_selection: The two crypto CFDs the crypto practice sleeve may trade (ADR-0049), Bitcoin and Ether, chosen before any result; they move together, so one trade is open at a time.
